description: local>kanso-labs/.github:renovate-config is the organization's shared Renovate preset, holding the settings that have to hold in every kanso-labs repository. It is listed last because a later preset wins a conflict with an earlier one: moved ahead of config:recommended it would be overridden by the very preset it exists to correct. This file is merged over the runner's config.js rather than inheriting from it, so extending the preset here is what carries an organization-wide setting into this repository at all. See the README in kanso-labs/.github.

packageRules.description: babel-plugin-react-compiler declares @babel/types ^7, and Babel 8 removed AssignmentPattern from the LVal alias. Under Babel 8 the compiler raises (BuildHIR::lowerAssignment) Expected object property value to be an LVal on every component with a defaulted destructured prop, and panicThreshold defaults to none, so it skips them silently. Lift this once a babel-plugin-react-compiler release declares Babel 8 support.

@vitejs/plugin-react declares @rolldown/plugin-babel as an optional peer at ^0.1.7 || ^0.2.0, which a 0.x caret keeps on its own minor, so Renovate's lockfile update failed on 0.3.0 and every check died at npm ci, as on #1869. The overrides entry in package.json points that peer at the root's own @rolldown/plugin-babel, so it moves on its own. plugin-react imports nothing from it: reactCompilerPreset returns a plain preset object that vite.config.ts and tsdown.config.ts hand to the root's copy, so tsc -b checks that object against the installed version's types and src/components/compiler.test.ts fails if the components stop arriving compiled.

typescript-eslint peers on typescript >=4.8.4 <6.1.0. Renovate's lockfile update fails on that conflict, so its TypeScript 7 pull request carries package.json alone and fails npm ci, and npm resolves it locally only by overriding the peer. It would not work if it did resolve: TypeScript 7 is the native Go port and has no compiler API yet, which typescript-eslint is built on, so admitting it is upstream work rather than a range to widen — typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint#10940. The eslint group matches typescript-eslint but not typescript, so this one name needs a rule of its own. Lift this once a released typescript-eslint admits TypeScript 7.
Grouped in .github/dependabot.yml under a duplicate 'react' key, so YAML dropped it and these were never actually grouped.

eslint-plugin-oxlint peers oxlint at a tilde range on its own minor, and is published hours to a day after it, or not at all: oxlint 1.74.0 never had one. Whenever oxlint landed first, Renovate's group carried it alone, its lockfile update failed on the peer, and every check died at npm ci, as on #1659. The overrides entry in package.json points the plugin's peer at the root's own oxlint, so oxlint moves on its own and the plugin follows when it is published. The plugin imports nothing from oxlint; it reads .oxlintrc.json to turn off the ESLint rules oxlint covers, so a minor apart costs at most a rule oxlint has just added being reported twice.

The runtime the components import and the compiler that rewrites those imports release together, and each pins the next exactly: @stylexjs/unplugin pins @stylexjs/babel-plugin, which pins @stylexjs/stylex. Bumped apart, the components would run one release's runtime over styles another release compiled, and the lockfile would carry a second copy of the runtime to satisfy the compiler's pin. Renovate's monorepo presets do not cover facebook/stylex, so nothing else groups them: @stylexjs/unplugin 0.19.1 arrived as a pull request of its own.
